sentences.text:
Mool Singh Sikarwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4
September, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:20668
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Gwalior

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Rajesh Kumar Gupta

On The 4 th Of September, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 7729 of 2014
 Mool Singh Sikarwar
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Vijay Kumar Agrawal - Advocate for the petitioner
 Shri Abhishek Bhadoriya - Public prosecutor for the re
 No.1/State.
 Shri Asha Ram Shivhare- Advocate for respondents No.2 
 Order

This petition has been filed by the petitioner under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. against the order dated 24.12.2013 passed by Sessions Judge, Morena in Criminal Revision No.148/2023 whereby the order dated 31.07.2013 passed by Judicial Magistrate First Class, Morena in unregistered complaint case No.0/10 was confirmed and the complaint filed by the petitioner under Sections 420, 465, 467, 469,
471 and 474 of IPC against the respondents No.2 to 4 was dismissed under Section 203 of Cr.P.C.
2.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner had filed a private complaint against the respondents No.2 to 4 in the Court of Judicial Magistrate First Class, Morena stating that on 03.01.1986 respondents No.2 to 4 executed a sale-deed of a plot bearing survey No.488 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20668 2 MCRC-7729-2014 situated Moja Jora Khurd in favour of the petitioner and in lieu of the above sale of plot, respondents No.2 and 3 have received consideration amount of Rs.10,000/- from the petitioner.
Thereafter, after receiving the possession from respondents No.2 to 4, petitioner has constructed a house on the aforesaid plot.

The said plot was also mutated in the name of petitioner in the revenue records, but in the year 1992, the Collector and other Officers of the local Administration of District Morena have demolished the house of the petitioner.

In respect thereof, petitioner has filed the F.A.151/2000 and vide judgment dated 06.05.2008 passed by this Court in which it is observed that the house which was constructed by the petitioner, was actually on the government land bearing survey No.559, not constructed the said house on a plot which is bearing survey No.488 purchased by the petitioner.

After the said judgment passed in first appeal, the petitioner has filed several complaints to the Police Authorities Mool Singh Sikarwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171500765/
1 against the respondents No.2 to 4 for the cheating/forgery committed by them.

sentences.text:
Meanwhile,
petitioner has also filed a private complaint before the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Morena under Sections 420, 465, 467, 469, 471 and 474 of IPC.

The Judicial Magistrate First Class, Morena, after recording the evidence of the petitioner and the witnesses under Sections 200 and 202 of Cr.P.C.
has dismissed the complaint vide order dated 31.07.2013.

Against the aforesaid dismissal, petitioner has again preferred the Criminal Revision before the Court of the Sessions Judge, Morena, which was got also dismissed by the Sessions Judge by passing the impugned order (dated 24.12.2013).

entities.text: Court of the Sessions Judge, Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Thereafter, aggrieved by the same, the petitioner has preferred this petition for setting aside the impugned orders NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20668 3 MCRC-7729-2014 and for taking cognizance in the case against the respondents No. 2 to 4.
3.

Learned counsel for the respondents No.2 to 4 has referred the paragraph 8 of the impungned order dated 24.12.2013 passed in Criminal Revision No.148/2013 that the High Court has decided in the First Appeal No.151/2000 filed by petitioner vide order dated 06.05.2028 and observed that the construction of house which was raised by the plaintiff/petitioner over the Survey No.559 is the government land and not the plot bearing Survey No.488 which was purchased by the petitioner.
However, it is the case of civil nature, therefore, this petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. is not maintainable and liable to be dismissed.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5.

This petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been filed in the year 2014 and respondents/authorities have demolished the house of petitioner in the year 1992 by stating that the plot on which petitioner has constructed his house is of government land.

Through this petition, the petitioner has prayed for setting aside the impugned orders dated 24.12.2013 passed by the Sessions Judge, Morena in Criminal Revision No.148/2023 and the order dated 31.07.2013 passed by Judicial Magistrate First Class, Morena in unregistered complaint case No.0/10.

It is the case of civil nature which is lingering on for the last twenty years and Trial Court has already decided aforesaid issue that the petitioner has constructed his house over the land which is found to be government land.

6. Therefore, keeping in view of the overall facts and circumstances of the case and after perusing t h e r e c o r d , i t i s n o t t h e c a s e w h e r e a n y r e l i e f c a n N E U T R A L C I T A T I O N N O .
2025:MPHC-GWL:20668 4 MCRC-7729-2014 be granted to the petitioner for invoking the inherent powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.
7.
Accordingly, this petition sans merits and is hereby dismissed.

(RAJESH KUMAR GUPTA ) JUDGE mani Mool Singh Sikarwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171500765/
2
